Part B
Situation
You are Nico Lin. You work for Events Horizon, a company which organises large public events. You are part of a committee responsible for organising the Victoria Cup, a professional women’s tennis tournament.
In order to promote the Victoria Cup to the public, the head of the Victoria Cup project team, Anthony Au, is keen to ensure that the tournament is a success.
You will listen to a Zoom meeting between a young tennis star called Lara Taranova, her agent Victor Laurent and Anthony Au.
Before the recording is played, you will have five minutes to study the Question-Answer Book and the Data File to familiarise yourself with the situation and the tasks.
Complete the tasks by following the instructions in the Question-Answer Book and on the recording. You will find all the information you need in the Question-Answer Book, the Data File and on the recording. As you listen you can make notes on page 3 of the Data File.
You now have five minutes to familiarise yourself with the Question-Answer Book and the Data File.

Subject: The Victoria Cup – Things to do
Sent: April 28 2021 10:18 AM
Dear Nico,
These are the three things that I’d like you to do in preparation for the Victoria Cup.
Volunteer Ball Kids
We have decided to choose Changing Young Lives to provide the volunteer ball kids for the Victoria Cup. You need to write an email to Gilbert at Refugee Sanctuary explaining:
Why we didn’t choose them i.e. which job requirements they don’t meet; ways that we can contribute to their charity and what Lara has offered to do.
You may want to start by looking at the notice we sent to the charities.
Letter to the Editor from Ms. Singh
You may have seen the letter to the editor in the Hong Kong Press & Journal from a Ms. Geeta Singh complaining about various issues. Please write a letter to the editor in response to Ms Singh’s letter reminding the readers of Ms Singh’s complaints and stating our responses to them. You may have to look at the transcript that Sana made of her conversation with Mr Barnes.
Email to PR Department about Promotional Poster
Our promotional poster for the Victoria Cup has received criticism. Please send an email to Alfred Roi at the PR department making sure that he understands exactly why the poster has to be redesigned.
You can start by looking at the Bon Accord News article.
Thanks again for your help.
Anthony Au, Project Leader, Events Horizon

Volunteer opportunities notice sent to Hong Kong charities
Events Horizon announce the following volunteer opportunity for charities in Hong Kong:
Ball Kids – Victoria Cup
Ball Kids – Victoria Cup (Period September 27 – October 3 2021)
Job description:
The main job of the ball kids is to retrieve tennis balls when they are out of play and to supply players with a towel and refreshments. They must perform these duties so that players and officials can concentrate without being distracted.
Requirements:
We are seeking a dynamic team of 100 ball boys and/or ball girls for the Victoria Cup. Both spoken English and Cantonese required.
Deadline to express an interest: 25 April 2021
If your charity would like to express an interest in taking part in the above, complete the Google Form on the Events Horizon website (www.events.horizon.com.hk).
Hong Kong Charity Google Forms
Name of Charity:Refugee SanctuaryArea of Hong Kong:Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong KongNumber of children:200Number of staff:15 full time staff and 35 volunteersContact person:Gilbert BayoOrganisation Description (100 words max.)
R.S. is a Hong Kong-based trust that looks after forced migrant children mainly from Africa and South East Asia. We provide a safe and supportive living environment for these vulnerable members of society who have fled dangerous and life-threatening situations, often becoming orphaned in the process. Some of our children speak English but very few of them can speak Cantonese so we help them to learn the basics of the language and integrate into Hong Kong society. The refugee children stay in our centre up until the age of 10, after which they go on to one of our partner charities.
Name of Charity:Changing Young LivesArea of Hong Kong:Shek Kip Mei, Hong KongNumber of children:500Number of staff:50Contact person:Emily ChanOrganisation Description (100 words max.)
The Changing Young Lives Foundation is committed to identifying talented underprivileged youngsters in Hong Kong and changing their lives for the better. We operate a coeducational learning institute in Shek Kip Mei where the brightest young people between the ages of 11 and 21 who would otherwise not be able to afford adequate schooling can come free of charge. Our children develop all the essential academic and social skills, becoming proficient in both English and Cantonese, and often going on to study at prestigious universities.

Minutes of the Victoria Cup Committee meeting
Date and time:Monday April 26th, 2021 at 2.00 pmVenue:Meeting Room 3b, Events Horizon Main OfficePresent:Tina Tong (TT); Sana Javed (SJ); Anthony Au (AA); Samuel Lo (SL)1. Confirmation of minutes
2. Charity donations
TT gave a brief presentation outlining the characteristics of the two charities Refugee Sanctuary and Changing Young Lives. A lengthy discussion ensued regarding the relative merits of both.
SJ proposed we give both of them 50 complimentary tickets. She commented that it would show goodwill. All agreed that this would be a nice gesture.
3. Volunteer Ball Kids
SJ informed the committee that having reflected on the safety issues and possible PR ramifications, the volunteer ball kids should be at least 11 years old. The committee agreed.
4. Corporate sponsor tickets
SL brought to our attention public discontent with the number of corporate tickets last year for our sponsors and suggested restricting the number of such tickets this year.
AA opined that this would be very difficult to do because tickets had already been issued. He also pointed out that only 12% of tickets went to corporate sponsors.
SJ proposed a condition of punctuality. He specified that corporate sponsor ticketholders should lose their ticket if they had not arrived within 60 minutes of the start of play. All agreed that this measure would be harsh but fair.
5. Fanzone
SJ provided an update on the Fanzone preparations. She reported that she had contacted the All England Lawn Tennis Club regarding their use of the Fanzone and ticket system there. SJ proposed adopting the same system at the 2021 Victoria Cup so that even more real fans can attend. The meeting unanimously accepted the proposal.
Next meeting to be held on Fri. 14 May at 2.00 pm.
There being no other business, the meeting finished at 4.25 pm.

Letter to the Editor of the Hong Kong Press & Journal from Ms. Geeta Singh
24th April, 2021
Dear Sir/Madam,
I am writing in regard to your article about the 2021 Victoria Cup which appeared in your newspaper on 21 April as I am keen for the organisers to avoid the mistakes they made last year regarding ticketing. First of all, last year, I was annoyed to find that the majority of the seats were reserved for corporate sponsors and their guests. As well as being unfair, I can also testify that a good number of these corporate sponsor seats are invariably left empty because they don’t show up.
Another issue last year was that us real fans could not get a hold of tickets whilst the people who actually got the tickets weren’t even real tennis fans. Ironically, it is exactly these people who end up talking through the matches and putting players off. I would like to know what Events Horizon intends to do about this type of spectator this year. We can’t go on like previous years when the stewards have been too scared to say anything.
For the benefit of the Hong Kong public and for the health of the sport in general, I urge Events Horizon to address these issues.
Yours faithfully,
Geeta Singh

Transcript of phone conversation between Sana Javed and Leon Barnes
Date: Mon, April 12, 2021
Leon:Hello. This is Leon Barnes from the All England Lawn Tennis Club at Wimbledon.
Sana:Hi Leon, this is Sana Javed from Events Horizon. We’re organising the Victoria Cup.
Leon:Oh yes, hi. I was expecting your call.
Sana:Just so you know, I’m recording the call so that I can transcribe it to share the information with my colleagues. Is that ok?
Leon:Yes, no problem.
Sana:Ok, so, I’m calling to pick your brains about on-the-day ticketing. I wonder how you handle the demand from the public for the biggest matches at Wimbledon. In Hong Kong we have a Fanzone in Victoria Park, where fans can catch the action on the large screen, but to be honest it hasn’t been a success. Last year there were really barely any fans there.
Leon:Right, well, at Wimbledon, we’ve found that the trick is to, you know, assure the fans that if they turn up on the day, they’ll have a chance to get a seat. You’d be surprised how many no-shows we get. Honestly, especially from the corporate sponsors. There’s no reason to waste a good seat, that’s what we say. So we give those tickets away to fans.
Sana:Wow. That sounds very good and everything but surely it causes a stampede!
Leon:Not quite! I mean, as the fans enter, I suppose you could say what is the equivalent of your “Fanzone” at Wimbledon, they’re given a ticket number as they come in. Our staff keep track of any seats that are not claimed and release them to the fans that have the lowest ticket numbers once it’s confirmed that the seats won’t be occupied.
Sana:Right, well thanks for the info. The use of the Fanzone’s an agenda item at our next committee meeting, so what you’ve just told will be useful for our discussion. I’m sure it’ll help.
Leon:No problem. Good luck and do let me know how it goes.

Bon Accord News article · 22 April 2021
Exclusive: Sponsor Joins Chorus of Criticism of Victoria Cup Advertising Campaign
Our reporter understands that Sportrite are considering withdrawing their corporate sponsorship of the Victoria Cup following a controversial poster campaign promoting the event. The poster in question featured an image of Suzie Gilmour, ranked number 80 in the world, posing according to one insider, “like an amateur model”. A spokesman for the company, Tim Lewis, revealed that the sponsors had made their expectations very clear to organisers Events Horizon:
“We have made it clear to Events Horizon that this was certainly not who we expected to be on the poster. We expected the highest-ranking player.” Mr Lewis added, “We requested a photo of the player in action on the tennis court, not posing like some sort of high fashion supermodel. At present we certainly don’t think the poster is aligned with our company’s aim and vision.”

Comments
Dan123There’s nothing wrong with using natural female beauty and elegance to attract fans to the event. Those who are criticising this poster are probably jealous that they will never be as beautiful or successful as this woman.
MarkW@Dan123 you are in the minority with your views on this. I doubt that you’re a real tennis fan. If they want to really create a genuine interest in women’s tennis as a sport, they should be using the player’s sporting talents and achievements, not their appearance, to promote their event to the public.
EekamouseRight on. Good to see some famous celebs saying the same. Check out this interview with Summer Li in Sonic Attack.

Interview with singer Summer Li from Sonic Attack online magazine
Sonic Attack Reporter:Summer, you have been known in the past for speaking up against what upsets you from the things you see. What’s upset you recently?
Summer:A good question. Lots of things. Oh I know, a poster I just saw for the Victoria Cup.
Sonic Attack Reporter:Really? I think I know which one you mean. What upset you most about it?
Summer:What upset me even more than the image on the poster was the slogan.
Sonic Attack Reporter:What was the slogan again? Something like “look like a woman, play like a man”?
Summer:Yes. I can barely repeat it. It makes me so angry.
Sonic Attack Reporter:Why? Why does it annoy you so much?
Summer:Well first of all, women shouldn’t feel that they have to look a certain way.
Sonic Attack Reporter:Yeah, totally.
Summer:I mean, to fit this narrow mainstream perception of beauty. You know the usual one we’re bombarded with. Plus, there’s no reason in the world why women tennis players should aspire to play like men.
Sonic Attack Reporter:Yeah I know, that’s such a lame thing to put.
Summer:You know, it’s like – as if that’s the best thing – the ultimate – the highest achievement a woman can achieve, to be like a man. Really! Who did the poster? Who are the promoters?
Sonic Attack Reporter:I think they’re called Events Horizon.
Summer:Yeah which century do they think they’re living in?
